first.rationale:
The competitive situation creates strong pull toward promotional_pricing, and memory_73 is exactly the memory that would justify it — which is why it is the first thing I want verified rather than acted on. It is also the most suspicious record in the set: it carries noticeably more specific claims than any sibling memory (acquisition AND revenue lift AND reduced time-to-first-value AND generalization across both billing plans). That pattern of accreted specificity is characteristic of a summary that has drifted across consolidations, and the original record may support a narrower claim (e.g., acquisition lift in one segment, with no retention or margin follow-up). Discount-led acquisition is precisely where short-term wins and 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' can diverge: it can pull in low-willingness-to-pay accounts, reset price expectations, and depress net revenue quality even while top-line signup metrics improve. I will not commit a pricing response to a competitor on an unverified secondhand summary.

Second verification goes to memory_86 because it underwrites my current intended action, and honest practice is to check the memory I am relying on, not only the one I am skeptical of. memory_31 and memory_86 may in fact be two consolidations of the same underlying onboarding experiment, in which case the apparent 'two independent sources' support for onboarding is illusory and I should downgrade my confidence accordingly. Verifying 86 tests that directly.

Current intent is simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale. It targets the two measured declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) at their mechanism rather than papering over them with price, it does not incur the margin and revenue-quality risk that pricing does, and a failure is cheap and reversible. This is explicitly provisional: if memory_73's source record turns out to be robust and includes retention/margin follow-up, promotional_pricing becomes defensible — but I would still run it as a small_guarded_test with revenue-quality and retention as gating metrics, not as a broad rollout. If memory_86's source is weak or duplicative of memory_31, I will drop to a smaller onboarding test rather than escalate scale on thin evidence. No direction here is being treated as settled; the inherited memories are plausible priors, not verified findings, and the competitive urgency is a reason to verify carefully, not a license to skip verification.
